project.name: Apollo
project.description: Apollo is a reliable, centralized configuration management system designed for microservice architectures. It enables teams to manage configurations across multiple environments, clusters, and applications through a unified interface. The system supports real-time configuration updates (hot releases), version management with rollback capability, grayscale deployments, and comprehensive audit logging. Apollo consists of a server-side built on Spring Boot and Spring Cloud, a framework-agnostic Java SDK, and a .NET SDK, making it suitable for heterogeneous microservice deployments.
project.architecture_summary: Apollo follows a distributed, multi-layered architecture. The server-side comprises four main components: Admin Service (configuration management backend), Config Service (client configuration delivery), Meta Service (service discovery), and Portal (web UI for administration). The architecture uses Spring Boot for service bootstrap and Spring Cloud for cloud-native patterns. A horizontally-scalable database backend stores configurations, audit logs, and metadata. The system implements service discovery abstraction supporting multiple backends (Eureka, Kubernetes, Nacos, Consul, Zookeeper), repository pattern for data access, and comprehensive audit trails with AspectJ AOP. The codebase is organized into domain modules (admin-service, config-service, meta-service, portal) with shared infrastructure for security, messaging, caching, and data access patterns.
